methodological_rigor.justification: Well-designed comparative liquid biopsy study of 58 LUAD patients (30 early-stage, 28 late-stage; 29 KRASmt/29 KRASwt) using sequential differential ultracentrifugation to isolate EV-enriched pellets (P1, P2, P3) and plasma supernatant (SUP). EV characterization uses appropriate multi-modal methods (western blot for Flotillin-1, CD9, albumin; TRPS for size distribution; TEM for morphology). ddPCR with Bio-Rad KRAS G12/G13 screening kit, false positive rate assay used to define >=3 mutant events threshold. Statistical analysis (Fisher's exact, Cohen's kappa, ANOVA) is appropriate. Limitations clearly acknowledged: small starting plasma volume (2.5 mL), pre-existing storage of P1/P2 vs later isolation of P3, no DNase treatment causing cfDNA contamination of pellets, EV characterization performed on only one representative sample, and no multiregional tumor sequencing for discordance cases.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy / case-control comparison of KRAS mutation testing across plasma fractions maps to Oxford LoE 3b. Clinical relevance is meaningful: KRAS G12C inhibitors (adagrasib/sotorasib) are now standard for advanced LUAD and rely on accurate mutation detection; liquid biopsy detection is actively evolving. The finding that SUP plasma (effectively cfDNA) outperformed EV-enriched fractions for sensitivity (92.9% in late-stage LUAD) challenges the prevailing enthusiasm for EV-based mutation testing in LUAD, a practically useful result. However, early-stage LUAD mutation detection remains poor across all fractions, limiting immediate translational value for screening.

reporting_quality.justification: STARD applies to this diagnostic accuracy study. Reporting is thorough: clear participant selection, flow of cases, clear index tests (ddPCR on P1, P2, SUP, P3), reference standard (tissue NGS), predefined positivity threshold (>=3 mutant events) based on false-positive rate assay, sensitivity/specificity/PPA/NPA/OPA/Cohen's kappa reporting, handling of discordant cases (L21 explored in depth), and explicit MISEV2023 acknowledgement for EV nomenclature. Western blot, TRPS, TEM methods described in detail. Limitations section is exemplary in transparency. Data availability score 3 because methods support reproducibility and raw data in supplementary tables are referenced.

novelty_literature.justification: EV DNA and cfDNA comparisons for mutation detection have been reported in colon (Choi 2022), pancreatic (Allenson 2017, Bernard 2019), NSCLC EGFR (Castellanos-Rizaldos 2018), and NSCLC WGS (Moldovan 2024). The specific comparison of four differential ultracentrifugation-derived plasma fractions (P1 large EVs, P2, SUP cfDNA, P3 small EVs) for KRAS G12/G13 in LUAD - including across early and late stages - is incremental but novel. The finding that SUP outperforms EV-enriched fractions in LUAD contrasts with pancreatic cancer findings and is a useful cross-cancer observation. Extension rather than breakthrough.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is clearly written, well-organized, and presents technically complex EV/molecular biology content in an accessible manner. Methods are sufficiently detailed for reproduction. Figures are well described. Discussion balances the findings against prior literature (Choi, Allenson, Castellanos-Rizaldos, Moldovan) and explores multiple explanations for discordant results (clonal hematopoiesis, tumor heterogeneity, subclone sampling). Limitations section is unusually candid. Minor issues: some repetition and a few awkward sentences.

key_strengths: Rigorous EV characterization with multi-modal validation (western blot, TRPS, TEM) aligned with MISEV2023 guidelines
Head-to-head comparison of four differential ultracentrifugation-derived plasma fractions for KRAS mutation detection in LUAD, a novel design
Predefined positivity threshold (>=3 events) based on false-positive rate assay supports analytic rigor
Clinically relevant finding that SUP plasma (cfDNA) outperforms EV-enriched fractions for KRAS detection in LUAD, contrasting with pancreatic cancer literature
Exemplary limitations section with transparent discussion of methodological caveats including sample volume, storage differences, and EV isolation purity
key_concerns: Early-stage mutation detection is effectively absent across all fractions (0%-6.7% sensitivity), limiting screening utility
EV characterization (WB, TRPS, TEM) performed on only one representative case rather than per-sample, limiting inter-sample validity of EV content
Pre-existing P1/P2 storage vs later P3 isolation introduces a methodological asymmetry not fully controlled
Small plasma volume (2.5 mL) likely limited cfDNA/EV DNA yield; authors acknowledge this
Results contrast with pancreatic cancer literature without a clear mechanistic explanation beyond methodology differences
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically careful, transparently reported comparative EV/cfDNA study with a practically useful negative finding for EV-based KRAS testing in LUAD. Fits Tier 3 with minor revisions.
